1989-2000.what: Two ordinary ground-floor windows on the front were replaced by a blank panelled shopfront with a sign board above it and a small wall box beside it
1989-2000.why: the ground floor was converted from living rooms to a shop or workshop; the blank panel may mean it is shut or shuttered

1989-2000.what: The three narrow, trimmed upper-floor windows on the front were replaced by wider, plain windows with no surround
1989-2000.why: a modernising window replacement by the owner; the ground-floor windows, door hood and flower boxes were left as they were

1989-2000.what: The boarded side and gable windows look slightly more weathered, with harder board and roof lines (seen from the steps only)
1989-2000.why: the house stayed empty and boarded, so it kept weathering

2000-2010.what: The boarded gable and side windows were opened and glazed again, and the cladding and roof look tidier, with the chimney a touch higher
2000-2010.why: someone moved back in or the owner repaired it

2000-2010.what: The gable window and the two lower front windows were boarded up with braced shutters
2000-2010.why: the house was left empty or abandoned, perhaps as C filled up

2000-2010.what: A railing or fence appeared at the left edge of the front, beside the bay and shopfront
2000-2010.why: an added balcony, terrace or safety rail for the shop; I cannot tell exactly what it is

A.claim: Before 1989 it was a well-built, well-trimmed two-storey house with an upper bay and an ordinary row of ground-floor windows, lived in as a home
Between 1989 and 2000 its ground floor was turned into a shop, with a sign board and a blank panel replacing two windows
Between 2000 and 2010 a railing was added at its left side
It was kept up the whole time: the roof, trim and upper windows stayed intact and nothing was boarded

B.claim: Before 1989 it was a neat house with narrow trimmed windows, flower boxes and a hooded door, looked after by its owners
Between 1989 and 2000 its upper-floor windows were replaced with wider plain ones, a modernisation
It has not changed since 2000 and stays well kept

C.claim: Before 1989 it was already empty: its side and gable windows were boarded in 1989 and 2000
It kept weathering while boarded, with the cladding and roof lines getting harder by 2000
Between 2000 and 2010 it was reopened, with the windows glazed and the cladding and roof tidied
From 2010 to 2020 it was lived in and kept

D.claim: Before 1989 and up to 2000 it was a lived-in, kept house with glazed, trimmed windows
Between 2000 and 2010 its windows were boarded up: it was vacated or abandoned
It was still boarded in 2020, so it stayed empty for at least a decade
A simple swap of occupancy with C: C became occupied as D became empty

E.claim: A small dark-clad house at the top of the lane, seen only at a distance; it looks lived in and glazed in every year
I saw no change to it between 1989 and 2020
